# google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user

Represents a Token Auth User for a Google Cloud Redis Cluster.


To get more information about ClusterTokenAuthUser, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.clusters)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/)

~> **Note:** Removing a `google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user` resource from the Terraform configuration deletes the user and revokes all of its tokens.

The `default` user is automatically created when token-based authentication (`AUTH_MODE_TOKEN_AUTH`) is enabled on a cluster and is lifecycle-bound to the cluster; it cannot be created or deleted via `google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user`. To view the `default` user's metadata, use the `google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user` data source.

## Example Usage - Redis Cluster Token Auth User Basic


```hcl
resource "google_redis_cluster" "user-basic-cluster" {
  name                        = "user-basic-cluster"
  shard_count                 = 1
  region                      = "europe-west4"
  authorization_mode          = "AUTH_MODE_TOKEN_AUTH"
  deletion_protection_enabled = false
}

resource "google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user" "user-basic" {
  cluster                     = google_redis_cluster.user-basic-cluster.name
  user_id                     = "user-basic-user"
  region                      = "europe-west4"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `cluster` -
  (Required)
  The name or resource ID of the Redis cluster.

* `user_id` -
  (Required)
  The unique ID (username) of the Token Auth User.
  The `default` user cannot be managed with this resource.


* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the region of the Redis cluster.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}`

* `name` -
  The full resource name of the Token Auth User.

* `state` -
  The current state of the Token Auth User.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


ClusterTokenAuthUser can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}`
* `{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import ClusterTokenAuthUser using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    region = "<-optional value->"
    cluster = "<-required value->"
    userId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ClusterTokenAuthUser using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}"
  to = google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ClusterTokenAuthUser can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default {{region}}/{{cluster}}/{{user_id}}
$ terraform import google_redis_cluster_token_auth_user.default {{cluster}}/{{user_id}}
```
